item.title: Homelab Chronicles: Keeping Things Up to Date
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
A couple of weeks ago I wrote about pinning every image in my homelab by digest and running a self-hosted Renovate on Docker Swarm. Since then the homelab has moved to k3s, and the update loop moved with it. Flux deploys from Git, Renovate runs as a CronJob, and konflate shows me what each pull request will actually change in the cluster before I approve it.

Flux, Trimmed Down

The nodes are small ARM boards, so memory decides most things. I don’t use Helm or Flux’s notifications, so I installed only the two controllers I need and committed the output, which lets Flux manage its own installation:

item.title: Killing :latest in My Homelab: Digest-Pinned Images and a Self-Hosted Renovate on Docker Swarm
item.author: xxxx
item.description:
My homelab runs on a small Docker Swarm: a few ARM single-board computers and an x86 box spread across two locations, joined over Tailscale. Every stack lives in a single Git repository, and Portainer’s GitOps sync deploys whatever lands on main. It is a setup I am genuinely happy with, except for one line that kept showing up in almost every stack file:

image: traefik:latest

Out of roughly forty images, most were pinned to latest. A handful were pinned to a version, and a few had no tag at all, which is the same thing as latest with less honesty.
